chapters.title: Chapter 3: Debt Markets and Interest Rates

lessons.title: Credit Ratings Explained: What CRISIL, ICRA and CARE Ratings Mean for a Business

children.text: A lender deciding whether to hand over ₹500 crore cannot personally investigate every borrower. Credit ratings exist to compress that judgement into a short code. Those codes decide what your company pays to borrow, which investors are even allowed to lend to it, and in some cases whether a customer should be given credit at all.

body.text: A credit rating answers exactly one question: how likely is this borrower to pay back on time? It says nothing about whether the shares are a good buy, whether the business is well run, or whether the price is fair.

children.text: Reading the Scale

markDefs.definition: An opinion issued by a registered agency on a borrower's ability and willingness to repay a specific debt obligation on time. It is an opinion on default risk, not a guarantee.
Ratings of BBB minus and above on the long-term scale. Many institutional investors are permitted to buy only investment grade paper, by regulation or by their own mandate.

children.text: A
credit rating

is issued by SEBI-registered agencies, including CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, India Ratings, Acuité, Brickwork and Infomerics. SEBI standardises the symbols, so an AA from one agency means the same broad thing as an AA from another. The critical dividing line on the scale is the
investment grade
cutoff.

cells: High safety, very low credit risk
Very high risk of default, default imminent
In default, or expected to be in default soon

body.text: Plus and minus modifiers refine the middle of the scale, so AA plus sits just below AAA and A minus just above BBB plus. Short-term instruments such as commercial paper use a separate scale running from A1 plus at the top down to A4, with D for default. Ratings also carry the agency's name as a prefix, which is why you see them written as CRISIL AAA or ICRA AA.

body.label: What D Actually Means
body.context: D is not a warning about the future. It records that payments have been missed. By the time a rating reaches D, the damage has happened, which is why the direction of travel matters more than the letter itself.

children.text: Why One Letter Is Worth Crores

body.title: Price the Upgrade
body.prompt: A company with ₹100 crore of borrowings is upgraded from A to AA. Using the indicative costs above, 9.0% falls to 8.2%. How much does it save in interest each year, in ₹ lakh?
body.explanation: The saving is 0.80 percentage points. ₹100 crore × 0.80% = ₹0.80 crore = ₹80 lakh a year, every year, for doing nothing except convincing an agency the business got safer. This is why finance teams treat rating meetings as seriously as board meetings.

children.text: The cost of borrowing is only the visible part. A downgrade below investment grade can also shut a company out of the market entirely, because many mutual funds, insurers and pension funds are simply not permitted to hold sub-investment grade paper. Forced selling by those funds then pushes the cost up further.
How a Rating Is Arrived At

events.title: The Company Appoints an Agency
events.description: The borrower mandates a rating agency and pays its fee. This issuer-pays model is standard globally and carries an obvious tension, which regulation tries to manage.

events.title: Data and Management Meetings
events.description: The agency examines financials, order books, group structure, banking conduct and repayment history, then meets management to test the plan behind the numbers.

events.title: The Rating Committee Decides
events.description: An internal committee, not the analyst alone, assigns the rating. The company can appeal with fresh information, but cannot simply demand a better grade.

events.title: Rationale Published
events.description: The agency publishes the rating with a written rationale setting out key strengths, weaknesses and what would trigger a change. This document is public and free to read.

events.title: Continuous Surveillance
events.description: The rating is monitored through the life of the instrument, with formal reviews and immediate action if something material happens, such as a missed payment or a large acquisition.

events.title: Outlook or Watch Changes
events.description: Before moving a rating, agencies usually signal direction by changing the outlook or placing the rating on watch. These early signals are the ones worth tracking.

columns.label: Outlook (Positive, Stable, Negative)
points: Indicates the likely direction over the medium term
Driven by gradual trends in performance or leverage
A negative outlook is a caution, not a decision
Can sit unchanged for several quarters

columns.label: Rating Watch
points: Signals a likely change in the near term
Usually triggered by a specific event, such as a merger, a large debt raise or a promoter dispute
Resolved once the event plays out, often within weeks or months
A sharper warning than an outlook change

body.title: What Agencies Are Actually Looking At

children.text: Rating rationales are long, but they almost always assess five things:
Business risk.
How stable is demand, how concentrated are customers, how cyclical is the industry, and how much pricing power does the company have.
Financial risk.
How much debt sits against profits, and how comfortably profits cover interest, measured through ratios the rationale will state explicitly.
Liquidity.
What is maturing in the next twelve months, and what cash, undrawn limits and expected inflows are available to meet it. Many defaults are liquidity failures rather than solvency failures.
Management and governance.
Track record, related party transactions, auditor changes, promoter share pledges and past repayment discipline.
Parent or group support.
Whether a stronger parent is expected to step in, which can lift a subsidiary's rating above what it would earn standalone, and drag it down if the parent weakens.

body.caption: The single ratio most often quoted in rating rationales: how many times over can profits cover the interest bill.

children.text: A company with ₹60 crore of operating profit and a ₹20 crore interest bill has coverage of 3 times. If profits fall to ₹30 crore while interest rises to ₹25 crore after a rate cycle, coverage drops to 1.2 times, and the rating conversation changes completely, without a single missed payment yet.

body.text: Ratings are opinions formed from available information, and they can lag reality badly. IL&FS carried top-tier ratings until shortly before its defaults in 2018. Treat a rating as one input, alongside the company's own disclosures, its payment behaviour with you, and plain commercial judgement. A rating is never a substitute for getting paid on time.

body.title: The Downgrade Domino
body.question: A listed company is downgraded from AA minus to BBB plus. Which of these is the least likely immediate consequence?
options: Its borrowing costs rise on refinancing
Some mutual funds have to reduce or exit their holdings of its debt
Its existing fixed rate bonds automatically start paying a higher coupon
Loan covenants linked to rating levels may be triggered
body.explanation: A fixed coupon is fixed for life. What changes is the market price of those bonds, which falls so that the yield compensates new buyers for higher risk. Everything else listed does follow a downgrade, and some loan agreements explicitly link pricing or repayment triggers to the rating.

body.title: Should We Extend ₹5 Crore of Credit to This Customer?
body.scenario: You head sales operations at an industrial components supplier. A large customer wants to move from advance payment to 90 day credit terms, on orders worth about ₹5 crore a year. Finance pulls the customer's rating: BBB minus with a negative outlook, downgraded twice in the last eighteen months. Sales is pushing hard, because the account is worth 8% of your revenue.
body.prompt: What does that rating tell you, what does it not tell you, and what would a sensible middle path look like?
body.modelAnswer: The rating tells you the customer is on the lowest rung of investment grade, with an agency signalling that the direction of travel is downward, and two downgrades already behind it. That is a genuine warning about the ability to pay on time, and 90 day unsecured credit at ₹5 crore of exposure is effectively lending to them at your own risk, without any of the protections a bank would insist on. What the rating does not tell you is whether the business is fundamentally viable, what their actual cash position is today, whether the downgrades reflect a group problem rather than this entity, or how they have behaved with you specifically, which is information you have and the agency does not. Read the published rating rationale, because it states exactly what drove the downgrades and what would trigger the next one. A sensible middle path avoids the binary. Start with shorter terms such as 30 days rather than 90, cap the outstanding exposure at a level you could absorb losing, ask for a partial advance or a bank guarantee on the balance, consider credit insurance or a factoring arrangement, and set a clear internal trigger to stop supply if payments slip. Also insist on monitoring: set an alert on further rating action, and review the account monthly rather than annually. If sales objects that this risks the relationship, the honest framing is that losing ₹5 crore of receivables would cost far more than losing the incremental margin on this account.

body.title: Quick Check
body.textWithBlank: On the long-term scale, the lowest rating still considered investment grade is ___ minus.
body.explanation: BBB minus is the floor of investment grade. One notch below, at BB plus, a large section of institutional money is no longer permitted to invest, which is why that single step down is far more expensive than any other on the scale.

body.title: How to Read a Rating Rationale in Ten Minutes
steps: Note the rating, the outlook and whether it is on watch, then check the previous rating to see the direction of travel
Read the key rating drivers section, where strengths and weaknesses are listed plainly
Find the liquidity paragraph, and compare debt maturing in the next year against available cash and undrawn limits
Read the rating sensitivities, which state exactly what would cause an upgrade or downgrade
Check what is actually rated, since a rating applies to specific instruments and facilities, not to the company as a whole
Look for group or parent support assumptions, because a rating can depend on someone else's willingness to help

cards.definition: The highest long-term rating, signalling the lowest expectation of default risk.
Ratings of BBB minus and above, the threshold many institutional investors are restricted to.
Default. Payments have been missed or are expected to be missed imminently.
The agency's view on the likely medium-term direction of a rating: positive, stable or negative.
A flag that a rating is likely to change soon, usually because of a specific pending event.
The convention that the borrower being rated pays the agency's fee, which creates a conflict that regulation and public rationales try to contain.
Ongoing monitoring of a rating through the life of the rated instrument, not just at issuance.
The highest short-term rating, typically seen on commercial paper issued by the strongest borrowers.
Operating profit divided by interest expense: how many times over profits can pay the interest bill.

body.label: Rating Agency Rationales
body.description: Rating rationales are published free on agency websites. Look up a large customer, a key supplier or your own employer, and read the liquidity and rating sensitivities sections. It is the most candid third-party assessment of a company you can get without paying for one.

points: A credit rating is an opinion on the likelihood of timely repayment, not a view on the share price or the quality of the business
The long-term scale runs from AAA down to D, and BBB minus is the investment grade floor that decides who is allowed to lend
A short-term scale, topped by A1 plus, applies to instruments like commercial paper
One notch of rating can be worth crores: an upgrade from A to AA on ₹100 crore of debt saves roughly ₹80 lakh a year at indicative spreads
Outlook signals medium-term direction and rating watch signals an imminent change, so both are worth tracking before the rating itself moves
Agencies weigh business risk, financial risk, liquidity, governance and group support, and publish the rationale free for anyone to read
Ratings lag reality and the issuer pays the fee, so use them as one input alongside your own commercial judgement, never as a guarantee

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute investment, credit or financial advice. Borrowing costs by rating are illustrative teaching figures, not market quotes. Rating symbols, definitions and disclosure requirements are prescribed by SEBI and by each agency, and change over time, so refer to the agency's own published scale for the current position.
